title: Sfumature Lessicali e Collocazioni
subtitle: Near-synonyms that aren't interchangeable, and the fixed word pairings native speakers expect.
objectives: Distinguish near-synonym pairs by register, connotation, or precise meaning
Avoid literal word-for-word translation from English collocations

content.intro: At C2, correctness alone isn't enough — native-like Italian depends on choosing the word a native speaker would actually reach for, in the exact combination they expect.
content.explanation: Many Italian near-synonyms differ by connotation, formality, or precise shade of meaning — not by strict correctness. Collocations (fixed word pairings, like English "heavy rain" rather than "strong rain") are equally important and rarely translate literally from English.

rules.heading: a) Near-synonym pairs
rules.body:
• lavoro (neutral) vs. occupazione (more formal/administrative) vs. impiego (a specific job/position)
  • felice (deep, meaningful happiness) vs. contento (satisfied, more everyday)
  • guardare (to look at, active) vs. vedere (to see, perceive)

rules.heading: b) Fixed collocations
rules.body: fare una domanda (to ask a question, not "chiedere una domanda"); prendere una decisione (to make a decision, not "fare una decisione"); commettere un errore (to make a mistake, not "fare un errore", though this is now widely tolerated); pioggia battente (pouring rain, not "pioggia forte").

examples.it: Mi ha fatto una domanda imbarazzante.
examples.en: He asked me an embarrassing question.

examples.it: Ha commesso un grave errore di valutazione.
examples.en: He made a serious error of judgment.

examples.it: Sono felice di essere qui con voi stasera.
examples.en: I am [deeply] happy to be here with you tonight.

commonMistakes.why: Decisions are "taken" (prendere), not "made" (fare), in standard Italian — a direct calque from English fails here.
Questions are "made/asked" with fare, not chiedere — chiedere una domanda is a common learner error, redundant in meaning too.

items.explanation: Prendere una decisione is the fixed collocation.
Fare una domanda is the fixed collocation.
Pioggia battente is the natural collocation for heavy, driving rain.

summary: Near-synonyms often differ by register or connotation rather than strict correctness — precise use is a C2 marker.
Collocations are fixed word pairings (prendere una decisione, fare una domanda) that rarely translate literally.
Direct calques from English collocations are one of the most persistent tells of a non-native speaker.
